structure: Part 11 read, in full, at commit 04a073b: the DR2.1 views review-notification.html, declaration.html, notification-submitted.html and delete-notification.html; the DR2.1 partials review-page-header.html, review-sections.html, review-summary-card.html, review-summary-row.html and delete-confirmation.html; and app/routes.js lines 4418-5776 (review value formatting, missing-field display, species and commodity sections, card error states, completeness, the review view model, read-only and cleared-error variants, DR2 commodity and document cards, review presentation, status-to-variant mapping, dashboard metadata, action-required warning, review page header), 5916-6194 (review page options and renderReviewNotificationPage, delete summary rows), 6267-6446 (delete page render, declaration date, validateDeclaration, conditional submission items, renderDeclarationPage, renderNotificationSubmittedPage) and 12046-12181 (GET/POST /review-notification, GET/POST /notifications/delete, GET/POST /declaration, GET /notification-submitted). Route handlers are written as root paths; app/lib/version-mount.js prefixes every redirect and rendered link with /design-release-2.1, so the claims give the bare path. Covered: the review page in its journey, draft (opened by reference), submitted, submission-complete and action-required variants, with its page header, import reference numbers, six numbered sections, every card and row with its label and change link, the missing-field display, every card error and the error summary; the POST from review and the completeness rule; the declaration page with every statement, the checkbox, its error and what submitting saves; the conditional items a submission carries; the notification-submitted page with every heading, panel, list and link; and the delete-notification page with its summary rows, question, buttons and POST. The journey variant's notification-status partial, the amend and cancel-amend modals and the copy-as-new and amend routes belong to other parts and are only referenced here.

claims.statement: The review page is reached at GET /review-notification and reads two optional query parameters: submitted (the id of a submitted notification) and reference (a notification reference).
When the review page is opened with a submitted id that matches no submitted notification, the user is redirected to the dashboard.

When the review page is opened with no submitted id and no reference, it shows the in-progress notification from the session in the 'journey' variant: editable, with change links, no page header, and a Back link to the notification hub.

claims.statement: A notification's status text maps to a review variant: 'submitted' to submitted; 'submission complete', 'complete' or 'completed' to submission-complete; 'submitted action required' or 'action required' to action-required; anything else, including draft, new and in progress, to draft. The match ignores case and surrounding spaces.

Looked up by reference, a submitted notification's status is 'Submitted action required' when it has conditional submission items and 'Submitted' when it has none, and its date is the date it was submitted.

claims.statement: Looked up by reference, a saved draft notification shows its own status text, or 'Draft' when it has none, always in the draft variant, dated by when it was created.

Every path the review, declaration, submitted and delete handlers redirect to or link to is served under /design-release-2.1, because the version mount prefixes redirects and rendered links with the release's base path.

claims.quote: To get help with import notifications for live animals or germinal products, email importsriskmanagement@apha.gov.uk.

claims.statement: The Getting help section reads 'Contact the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) if you need technical help with this service:' with the bullets 'Telephone: 0330 041 6999' and 'Email: APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk' (an email link).
claims.quote:

claims.statement: The Getting help section gives the opening hours 'Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5pm, except bank holidays'.
claims.quote: Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5pm, except bank holidays

claims.statement: The Getting help section reads 'If you need help with your customs declaration, contact HMRC.', where 'contact HMRC' opens the GOV.UK HMRC customs, international trade and excise enquiries page in a new tab.
claims.quote: If you need help with your customs declaration, contact HMRC.

claims.statement: The Getting help section ends with a 'Find out about call charges' link to https://www.gov.uk/call-charges, opening in a new tab.
claims.quote: Find out about call charges

claims.statement: The new-tab links on the submitted page do not tell the user they open in a new tab.
claims.note: Neither link text includes '(opens in new tab)'.

claims.statement: The delete-notification page is at GET /notifications/delete and needs a submitted id or a reference in the query; without one, or outside a design-release session, it redirects to the dashboard.
When the reference is the notification currently being worked on and is not yet saved anywhere, the delete page still opens, with its Back link and 'No, cancel' going to the review page.
When the submitted id or reference matches no notification and is not the one being worked on, the delete page redirects to the dashboard.
For a saved notification, the delete page's Back link and 'No, cancel' go back to that notification's view from the dashboard.
The delete-notification page shows the Alpha phase banner and a 'Back' link.
The delete-notification page heading is 'Delete this notification?'.
The delete-notification page shows a summary list with the rows 'Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number' and 'Origin'.

The delete page's Commodity row lists each commodity's common name with its species' Latin names in brackets, comma-separated (for example 'Cattle (Bison bison, Bos taurus)'); for 'other live mammals' each species' common name is used.
claims.note: The example names are illustrative, not taken from the source.

claims.statement: The delete page's Number row shows the total number of packages for a germinal-products-only notification, and otherwise the total number of animals.
The delete page's Origin row shows the country of origin.
A delete page summary row with no value from the notification falls back to the dashboard's listing for it, and shows 'Not applicable' when that is empty too.
Below the summary the delete page reads 'Confirm that you want to delete this notification.' and 'This action cannot be undone.'
claims.quote:
{{ confirmText }}

This action cannot be undone.

claims.statement: The delete page has a red 'Yes, delete' button that posts to /notifications/delete with the same submitted id or reference.
Beside 'Yes, delete' the delete page has a 'No, cancel' link going to the same place as the Back link.
Confirming the delete removes the notification identified by the submitted id or reference.
Deleting the notification currently being worked on also clears the in-progress journey from the session.
After a delete, the user is returned to the dashboard with the success message '<reference> has been deleted', or 'Notification has been deleted' when the reference is not known.
claims.quote:
req.session.data.dashboardSuccessMessage = notificationReference
    ? `${notificationReference} has been deleted`
    : 'Notification has been deleted'

claims.statement: The delete POST does not check that the notification exists or that the session is a design-release session before deleting and showing the success message.
claims.note: Unlike GET, POST has no redirect for a missing or unknown id; it always sets the success message.

claims.statement: The source says nothing about deleting a notification that has already been submitted beyond the same confirmation: no rule limits delete to drafts, and the review header offers Delete for every status.
claims.note: Looked in the review header, the delete GET/POST handlers and the delete partial for any status-based restriction or different wording for submitted notifications; found none.

claims.statement: The 'Copy' buttons in the Import reference numbers section carry the text to copy, but the slice does not show what the user sees after copying (no confirmation message).
claims.note: The copy behaviour is wired by front-end script outside this part's read list; no confirmation copy appears in the views read.
